checks.name: database
checks.details: 14 business tables, 78647 fixture records; every bound object returns its fixture row count, plus the package's DB verification hook; the plan dataset holds 13 history plans.

checks.name: knowledge
checks.details: 14 objects (13 table-bound, 1 dataset-bound) and 21 relations; all 605 production plans reach their products; the same after uninstalling and reinstalling.

checks.name: capabilities
checks.details: the Workshop app (Demand Forecast view / Production Line view) was created and published on the sample's network with its rule functions resolved to this installation's toolbox, and created again after reinstalling; through the toolbox proxy a demand-view batch of 15 plans and 20 unscheduled demands gave each demand the answer its detail gives, and the line check answered not applicable for tasks without a line; 4 mounted functions (2 calculations, 2 schedule rules) ran through execute_tool before and after reinstalling; the rule tools also answered through the toolbox proxy with check and detail; create, repeat create (updated, no new plan), adjust, cancel and whole-bill create ran as object actions and wrote the plan dataset; 2 Skills checked against source contents; no metrics.

checks.name: scenario
checks.details: 7 reference Cypher queries passed; the other 8 cards were not exercised as full questions; no model score or browser UI claim.

limits: Native execution covered Linux arm64 with an OpenBKN 0.2.2 main build (bkn-backend-ee sha2d2a597, ontology-query-ee with bkn-foundry#3125, agent-retrieval sha2d466bc, sandbox 0.2.2 main eeffdb4, sample service 022-3be0e6b3 with bkn-samples#285); no native amd64 certification and no released vanilla 0.2.2.

Calculations and schedule rules are mounted functions run through Context Loader execute_tool in a managed interaction; the rule tools were also called through the toolbox proxy without an interaction, as the schedule Gantt calls them. The plan actions ran through get_action_info, execute_action and get_action_execution.
Writing plans needs the OpenBKN 0.2.2 sandbox deployment (BKN_BASE_URL, BKN_TOKEN, gateway allowed); uninstalling needs a sample service with bkn-samples#260.
Delaying a purchase order on the platform was not exercised; the confirmed plans turning short when their purchase is delayed is covered by the source tests on the same fixtures.
The Workshop app needs the professional edition (Workshop); a community edition platform installs the sample without it, which was not exercised here.
The app's two pages were opened and its rule checks run in the browser on 8081; dragging plans and applying a scenario in the app were not exercised.
Reference queries, functions and actions were checked through APIs; full model-question cards were not exercised.

Kit check through the toolbox proxy, measured in the sandbox, three runs each: one plan's detail 3.04–3.06 s, the 13 installed plans 3.04–3.06 s, 200 plans 3.59–4.06 s. Most of the remaining time is the knowledge-network read of the BOM and sandbox start-up.

The same package was installed again after earlier attempts stopped on the test environment, not the sample: the command-line sign-in expired during the run, so the install hook was refused. The reported run passed every step.
